notes: TWO BLOCKS FOR FIVE CONTENT BANDS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DECISION ON THIS ROUTE. The page
has exactly five `sections` rows — tour, technology, expect, visit, faq, in the order the
template draws them, verified against the live endpoint on 2026-08-29. Two are claimed here
(#visit, #faq). The other three keep their template markup, unguarded, on both sides of the
switch, and keep reading their `sections` rows LIVE — they are listed under
`exempt.sections` with an un-defer condition each, and unlike a code_section exemption they
freeze nothing.
THE THREE UNMIGRATED BANDS LEAD THE PAGE, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON LEAVING THEM UNGUARDED IS
SAFE. #tour, #technology and #expect all sit ABOVE #visit, the first block, so a block run
that starts at #visit leaves the three exactly where they were. The mirror image of
general-dentistry's `.closing`, which is safe only while its `faq` block stays LAST. Put a
block above #tour — in wp-admin, by reordering — and this becomes the LocalTrust fault at one
remove: the three template bands would stay at the top while their neighbours moved below
them. Recorded again in `known_gaps` on the `visit` block, which is the block they now depend
on being first.
BAND VOCABULARY IS INVERTED ON THIS SHEET, as it is on the pilot and on the four hubs.
`.section.alt` is CHARCOAL (our-office.css:100) and `.section.dark` is SAGE-PALE
(our-office.css:113). Both `band` values below are resolved from those two rules, not from
the class name: reading the class would put a dark band under #faq and a pale one under
#visit, which is exactly the defect a word-level diff cannot see (src/lib/page-content.ts,
`unwrapSelects`).
NO RAIL ON THIS PAGE. `tocLinks` comes back null from the endpoint and the template has no
`.toc` nav at all, so every `nav_label` resolves blank through the map's default
({ toc_label: true } with no matching row), which keeps both blocks out of a rail that does
not exist. No derived-TOC loop was added to the template — one would feed nothing.
#visit IS A LAYOUT, NOT A code_section, AND THE ANSWER BINDS /contact/ TOO. Both pages ship
this band character for character (our-office/index.astro:318-384 and
contact/index.astro:288-357), and on BOTH of them the eyebrow, heading and body come from a
live `sections` row — five editable values between the two pages. A code_section freezes
exactly those, and the bands the escape hatch is for are the ones whose copy is ALREADY in
code. So it is the `map_visit` layout registered in cms/mu-plugins/vs-content-model.php
(:4725) and src/blocks/manifest.ts (:1081). Everything else in the band — street, city,
phone, email, opening hours, both buttons, the map embed — is site data and resolves from
src/data/contact.ts and src/data/hours.ts inside the component, never from a field.
THE COMPONENT THIS ROUTE DEPENDS ON HAS LANDED, and it is not in this agent's two files.
src/blocks/MapVisitBlock.astro now exists and PageFieldsBlocksMapVisitLayout is bound to it
in src/blocks/registry.ts:75. Re-read after this map was written, and it satisfies every
line of the contract below: no `data-vs-reveal-batch` on the <section>, both reveal hooks on

the two columns, `

` and no `.section-head`, `light` on the eyebrow only for
the sage-pale and sage bands, aria-label omitted entirely when blank, and the address line
built as ONE `${addressCity}, ${addressState} ${addressZip}` expression. Written as a
statement of fact rather than deleted: a gap note that still says "cannot" after it can is
how two real losses started on this project.
THE `expectTiles` CARDS ARE LIVE IN WORDPRESS AND THE TEMPLATE HAS NEVER READ THEM. Four
rows, group `expectTiles`, verified on the endpoint; the template hardcodes the same four
tiles as a local array (:90-111) because `.expect-tile` carries a FontAwesome icon and no
card row can hold one. The CMS text and the template text are word-for-word identical today
— checked, not assumed — so nothing is drifting, but the rows are unclaimed and are exempted
below rather than left for the leftover check to refuse.

blocks.band_evidence: our-office/index.astro:318 <section class="section alt" id="visit"> — our-office.css:100 — .vs-office .section.alt { background: var(--vs-charcoal-green); color: #fff }. `.alt` is the DARK one on this sheet; the header comment at :99 says so in as many words.

aria_label.from_template: our-office/index.astro:318 — the section's own aria-label. Stored rather than derived because /contact/ writes "Visit our practice" on the identical band (contact/index.astro:288) and nothing else on the row tells the two apart. Blank must emit NO attribute: aria-label="" strips a landmark's accessible name instead of leaving it to the heading.

blocks.layout_evidence: .vs-office .location-grid is grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr with align-items: stretch (our-office.css:326-329) — the copy-beside-map split this layout draws. The map cell is .location-map-wrap at aspect-ratio 4/5 (:407-414), not an image frame.
blocks.body_is_lede_note:
sections.visit.body -> `body`, and the component must draw it as `

` (our-office/index.astro:324), NOT as a bare

inside a `.section-head`. This band has no `.section-head` at all: the eyebrow, the h2 and the lede sit directly in `.location-copy` (:321-324). our-office.css:339 re-asserts the charcoal colour on `.section.alt .location-copy .lede` precisely because `.lede` at (0,3,1) outranks `.section.alt p` at (0,3,0) — the component owns both sides of that in its own scoped CSS and inherits neither.
blocks.eyebrow_class_note: THIS PAGE LOSES NOTHING HERE AND /contact/ LOSES ONE TOKEN. our-office writes a plain <span class="eyebrow"> on this charcoal band (:322) while contact writes <span class="eyebrow light"> (:292). MapVisitBlock follows the house rule every other block follows — `light` only on the sage-pale and sage bands — so this route matches byte for byte and /contact/ drops that one class. Colour is unchanged either way: the block owns the charcoal eyebrow colour in its own scoped CSS. Recorded in src/blocks/manifest.ts:1067-1073 as an expected normalisation.
blocks.reveal_note: THE SECTION ITSELF CARRIES NO `data-vs-reveal-batch`, unlike every other band on this page. The reveal attributes sit on the two children: `data-vs-reveal-batch` on .location-copy (:321) and `data-vs-reveal` on .location-map-wrap (:373). A component that put the batch attribute on the <section> would re-time the whole band's animation and change three attributes in the diff.
blocks.site_data_note: NO cta fields, no address fields and no hours rows, deliberately. The two buttons are variant="light" -> directionsHref hoverLabel "Open Map" and variant="ghost-light" -> phoneHref hoverLabel "Tap to Dial" (:368-369), the address rows and the hours table read src/data/contact.ts and src/data/hours.ts (:326-364), and the iframe src is built from addressLine (:37, :375-380). Storing any of them would be a per-band copy of a phone number, which is the whole of the href policy in block_cta_fields().
blocks.address_line_note: THE ADDRESS LINE MUST BE BUILT AS ONE EXPRESSION. The template writes {addressCity}, {addressState} {addressZip} as three spliced expressions (:331); compressHTML collapses the whitespace text node between two of them, which is how "Parker, CO80134" shipped on three live pages. The component builds `${addressCity}, ${addressState} ${addressZip}` as a single template literal. The output is the corrected string, so this route gains the same one-space correction the three hub `area` bands already took.
known_gaps: THIS BLOCK MUST STAY FIRST OR THREE TEMPLATE BANDS LAND IN THE WRONG PLACE. #tour,
#technology and #expect (our-office/index.astro:199, :253, :295) are unguarded template
markup that no registered layout expresses. They render above whatever PageBlocks draws,
which is correct only while this block is the first row in the list. Reorder in wp-admin so
any band precedes `visit` and the three stay pinned at the top while their neighbours move
below them. Their un-defer conditions are on `exempt.sections`; until one of them is met,
an editor reordering this page can produce a wrong order that nothing warns about.
CLOSED — the component gap this note described is filled. src/blocks/MapVisitBlock.astro
exists and is bound at src/blocks/registry.ts:75, and it honours the four notes above
(`body_is_lede_note`, `eyebrow_class_note`, `reveal_note`, `address_line_note`) as written.
The layout was already registered in vs-content-model.php (:4725) and manifest.ts (:1081),
so the window in which this band would have drawn UnknownBlock is shut. The map was still
written first on purpose, so the component had a written contract to satisfy.
AND THE PHP MUST REACH THE CMS HOST BEFORE THE NEXT BUILD. The manifest now selects
`ariaLabel` on PageFieldsBlocksMapVisitLayout; against a host still running the
pre-Wave-B vs-content-model.php the capability probe (src/loaders/pages.ts:191-266) throws
and all 48 routes fail to build. Standing PHP-before-manifest order, armed now.

blocks.band_evidence: our-office/index.astro:387 <section class="section dark" id="faq"> — our-office.css:113 — .vs-office .section.dark { background: var(--vs-sage-pale); color: var(--vs-ink) }. `.dark` is the LIGHT one on this sheet; the comment at :111-112 states the flip.

eyebrow.from_template: our-office/index.astro:390 — Office FAQ. Transcribed, not moved: sections.faq.eyebrow is NULL on the live endpoint, so the template's own string is the only copy of it. FaqBlock re-derives the `light` token from the band (eyebrowLight is true for sage-pale), so the class comes back on its own.

blocks.body_decision:
NOT SET, and blank is correct. sections.faq.body is null on the live endpoint and the template draws no

in the head (:389-392), so FaqBlock's `body &&` guard emits nothing — the same shape either way.
blocks.pull_decision: NOT SET. This page has no `.pull` aside; the hub variant maps sections.faq.body -> `body` and the ten detail routes map it -> `pull`, and this row has neither because the source is null. Writing it to `pull` would invent an aside the page has never had.
blocks.cta_decision: NO CTA FIELDS. The template's FAQ band ends at with no button row (:394-402); the closing call to action on this page is below it, which is chrome and not a block. FaqBlock's `hasCta` is false for a blank cta_label, so it draws no .cta-row and no phone button — including no `cta_phone_first`, which is an emergency-dentistry field and stays off this row.

items.note: All 4 rows, in order, MOVED — nothing here is transcribed. Row 1 is the only one with open=true, which the template passes through as `open={f.open}` (:396) and FaqBlock as `open={f.open ?? false}`. Row 4's answer carries an inline <a href="/new-patients/">; FaqBlock renders answers with set:html (its `.answer` div), exactly as the template does at :398, so the anchor survives. Verified against the endpoint on 2026-08-29: this page's answers contain one tag and no bare `<` or `&`, which is the pre-flight FaqBlock's header requires before an escaped-FAQ template becomes this block. NOTE the anchor has no class — the page sheet styles `.faq .answer a` positionally (our-office.css:470-474) and FaqBlock does not carry that rule, so the link renders in body colour rather than sage. Listed in known_gaps.

known_gaps: ONE CLASS TOKEN IS LOST ON THE HEAD, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS PROJECT HAS SEEN IT.
The template writes <div class="section-head center"> (:389); FaqBlock emits
<div class="section-head"> and centres in its own scoped CSS (`text-align: center`,
`margin: 0 auto 64px`). No previously migrated page used the `center` modifier — the four
hubs and the eleven detail pages all write a bare `.section-head` — so this is new to Wave
B and four other Wave-B routes carry the same token. The centring survives and so does the
eyebrow's second flanker: our-office.css:136-138 adds the ::after only under
`.section-head.center`, while FaqBlock draws ::before AND ::after unconditionally, so the
eyebrow still reads "— OFFICE FAQ —". Recorded here so the class-level comparison
(scripts/vr-html.mjs) has an expected difference to match rather than a surprise.
THE ACCORDION'S SURFACE COLOURS ARE BLOCK-OWNED AND DIFFER FROM THIS SHEET. The page sheet
draws the list on a translucent white over the sage-pale band — background
rgba(255,255,255,.55), borders rgba(0,0,0,.12) and .1, and rgba(255,255,255,.75) when open
(our-office.css:424-450). FaqBlock draws #fff, var(--vs-line), and var(--vs-cream) open.
The block's rules are two compounds deep under its own scope attribute, so they win
outright and the page sheet's copies go unused — no tie, nothing decided by bundle order.
Visible as a slightly more opaque card. Same normalisation the eleven detail routes took;
recorded rather than argued, and undone by the stylesheet pass, not by this map.
ONE MORE, SMALLER: our-office.css:470-474 colours `.faq .answer a` sage with an underline.
FaqBlock has no `.answer a` rule at all, so row 4's /new-patients/ link renders in
var(--vs-ink-soft) with the global anchor treatment. One link, one colour, on one page —
but it is a real difference and it belongs to whoever owns FaqBlock, not to this route.
<VirtualConsult> DEPENDS ON THIS BLOCK STAYING LAST, in the mirror of the dependency the
`visit` block carries. It is chrome (spec 7) and stays unguarded at :406, after everything
PageBlocks draws — which is the right place while `faq` is the last row. Unlike
general-dentistry's `.closing` this one is a component with no page copy of its own, so a
reorder misplaces a band rather than losing words; it is still a reorder nobody is warned
about.
THE FAQPage JSON-LD IS REBUILT ON THE PAGE, and that is not optional. Structured data
lives on the page, not in the band, so FaqBlock cannot own it; left reading `faqs` the
script would keep describing the pre-migration list the moment an editor reorders or
deletes a question inside the block. our-office/index.astro now derives `faqEntities` from
the block's own `items` when hasBlocks and from `faqs` otherwise — element for element, so
the else-branch payload is byte-identical to the pre-migration build. The Dentist and
BreadcrumbList payloads (:412-438) read only site data and are unchanged on both sides.

_: Every repeater row on this page that no block above claims. The backfill fails, before
writing anything, on any row that is neither claimed nor listed here.
THE THREE `sections` ENTRIES BELOW ARE NOT THE USUAL KIND. On the four hub routes an
exempt `sections` row means a code_section took its band and froze its copy. Here it means
the opposite: the band is still TEMPLATE markup on both sides of the switch, so the row
keeps feeding the page live and an editor's changes keep landing. Nothing freezes on this
route. What is lost is reorderability, not editability — and each entry names the one
change that would end the deferral.

sections.reason: The 5-tile image bento (our-office/index.astro:199-250). No registered layout carries a bento, and code_section is worse than useless here: a code-owned component cannot reach the page's `images` repeater, so the five CMS attachments would be unrenderable. Stays template markup, unguarded, still reading sections.tour live.
read_this_before_running: NOTHING FREEZES. Eyebrow, heading and body still come from this row at :202-204 after the
back-fill, exactly as they do today.
Un-defer condition: a layout with an images repeater whose rows carry a grid-area name.
The bento is a fixed 4x3 areas grid with named tiles a/b/c/d/e (our-office.css:185-209), so
the tile count is part of the design, not a column choice — a five-slot layout, not a
generic gallery. gallery_marquee is a scrolling strip and does not carry it.

read_this_before_running: The CMS text and the template text are identical today, word for word, checked against the
endpoint on 2026-08-29: "Free on-site parking", "Ground-floor entrance", "Calm, modern
interior", "300+ five-star reviews", with matching bodies. So no editor edit is being

widen. It closes with the same one change as #expect: an `icon` sub-field on card_grid.

images_decision: ALL NINE SLOTS ARE EXEMPT AND NONE IS UNCLAIMED-BY-ACCIDENT, which is the opposite of the
state /general-dentistry/ was deliberately left in. There the four service-tile slots were
left off this list so the planner would REFUSE the route rather than ship photo-less cards;
here every slot belongs to a band that is still drawn by the template, so every one keeps
rendering from the same line it renders from today. Neither block on this route has an
exempt.faqs_note: EMPTY BECAUSE ALL FOUR ROWS ARE CLAIMED by the `faq` block above, not because they are excused.
exempt.process_steps_note: `processSteps` comes back null from the endpoint. This page has no numbered-process band.
toc_links_decision: EMPTY BECAUSE THE PAGE HAS NO SUCH ROWS. `tocLinks` is null on the endpoint and the template
renders no `.toc` nav, so both blocks' nav_label resolve blank through the map default
({ toc_label: true } with no matching row) and neither appears in a rail. The leftover check
only reports rows that exist, so an empty list is correct and would start reporting the day
somebody adds a rail to this page — which is the behaviour worth keeping.
